title: Two-step generation of monodisperse agarose-solidified double emulsions (w/w/o) excluding an inner oil barrier
author: Brinkmann, Oberpaul, et al.

steps.title: Prepare all reagents and solutions
steps.instruction: Make the following solutions: (a) 20 mL Novec™ 7500 with 1 % (w/w) Pico‑Surf™ 1 by mixing 4 mL Pico‑Surf™ 1 (5 % w/w in Novec™ 7500) with 16 mL Novec™ 7500; (b) 40 mL distilled water; (c) 3 % (w/v) SeaPrep agarose in water (3 g SeaPrep in 100 mL water), autoclave, then stir at 60 °C with a magnetic stirrer until homogeneous; (d) 20 % (w/v) Nycodenz® (10 g in 50 mL water) and 30 % (w/v) Nycodenz® (15 g in 50 mL water); (e) 70 % (v/v) HPLC‑grade isopropanol. Filter every solvent through a 0.2 µm CA syringe filter before use.

steps.title: Set up microfluidic hardware
steps.instruction: Fill pump 1 and pump 3 reservoirs with water and pump 2 reservoir with the Novec™ 7500 + 1 % Pico‑Surf™ 1 prepared above. Turn on the air‑compressor and set pressure to 500–700 kPa. Power on the three pressure pumps, the temperature‑control unit (TCU), the illumination source and the computer. Launch the Flow Control Center (FCC) software and the Pixelink Capture software after the hardware is on. Set the TCU to 30 °C to keep low‑melting agarose liquid.

steps.title: Prime microfluidic channels
steps.instruction: Connect the Linear Connector to the reservoir chip. Apply a flow of 5 µL min⁻¹ to each of the three channels for 5 min to prime the system and purge air bubbles. Then set all flow rates to 0 µL min⁻¹ and disconnect the Linear Connector. Empty both sample reservoirs on the sample‑reservoir chip.

steps.title: Load first‑phase sample
steps.instruction: Prepare a loading suspension for a 1.5 % (w/v) agarose first phase by mixing 200 µL 3 % SeaPrep agarose solution with 200 µL water (or cell‑containing medium). Vortex 10 s. Load ≈90 µL of this mixture into each reservoir of the reservoir chip, then add 5 µL Novec™ 7500 on top of each loaded sample to keep it separated from the water front. Close the chip lid and reconnect the Linear Connector.

steps.title: Generate first‑phase droplets
steps.instruction: Set flow rates: pump 1 and pump 3 (sample) to 2 µL min⁻¹ each, pump 2 (oil) to 40 µL min⁻¹. Expected pressures are 350–550 mbar for oil and 550–800 mBar for water; do not exceed 1 200 mBar on any single pump. Wait 2–3 min for pressure stabilization, then collect the emerging w/o droplets in a 1.5 mL reaction tube for ~25 min (stop when a pressure drop indicates the reservoir is empty). After collection, set all pumps to 0 µL min⁻¹.

steps.title: Solidify first‑phase droplets
steps.instruction: Incubate the collected droplet suspension at 8 °C for 20 min to gel the agarose inside the oil droplets.

steps.title: Clean and sterilize chips after first phase
steps.instruction: Disconnect the Linear Connector and empty both reservoirs. To remove residues, pipet water up and down in each reservoir, then add 70 % isopropanol. Load both reservoirs with 70 % isopropanol, close the lid, reconnect the Linear Connector, set all pumps to 7 µL min⁻¹ and run for 10 min. Afterwards load both reservoirs with water, close the lid, reconnect, set pumps to 7 µL min⁻¹ and run another 10 min. Finally stop all pump flows. For long‑term storage dry or empty all channels and shut down the compressor, power, and computer.

steps.title: Break first‑phase emulsion
steps.instruction: In the 1.5 mL tube containing agarose droplets and the bottom Pico‑Surf™ 1 oil layer, remove as much oil as possible with a pipet. Add 250 µL Pico‑Break™ 1, gently invert to mix (solution turns orange). Centrifuge at 1 000 × g for 1 min to separate clear aqueous and orange fluorous phases.

steps.title: Perform density‑gradient centrifugation
steps.instruction: Tilt the tube to 45°, pipet off most of the orange fluorous phase. Add 500 µL water (or cell‑specific medium) to the remaining aqueous phase and transfer to a 15 mL centrifuge tube. Carefully underlay 2 mL of the 20 % Nycodenz® solution, then 1 mL of the 30 % Nycodenz® solution beneath it. Centrifuge at 2 000 × g for 1 min (do not exceed this speed).

steps.title: Extract and wash droplet layer
steps.instruction: Using a needle attached to a 1 mL syringe, pierce the tube just below the droplet layer (which sits atop the 30 % Nycodenz) and withdraw the agarose droplets. Transfer the clear droplet suspension to a fresh 1.5 mL tube. Centrifuge at 1 000 × g for 1 min and discard supernatant until ~200 µL remains (droplet pellet may be hard to see). Wash the pellet by adding 1 000 µL water (or medium), centrifuge again at 1 000 × g for 1 min, and discard supernatant until ~100 µL remains. The washed droplet layer is now ready for the second encapsulation.

steps.title: Prepare second‑phase loading suspension
steps.instruction: Mix 100 µL 3 % SeaPrep agarose solution with approximately 100 µL of the washed, oil‑free droplet layer obtained above.

steps.title: Generate double‑emulsion droplets
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 2.2–2.5 of the first‑phase protocol: vortex the new suspension 10 s, load ~90 µL into each reservoir, add 5 µL Novec™ 7500 on top, close the lid and reconnect the Linear Connector. Set flow rates: pumps 1 and 3 to 2 µL min⁻¹, oil pump 2 to 15 µL min⁻¹ (oil pressure 450–650 mbar, water pressure 800–1 100 mBar; max single pump 1 400 mBar). After a 2–3 min pressure stabilization, collect droplets for ~25 min, then stop all pumps (0 µL min⁻¹). Incubate the collected double‑emulsion suspension at 8 °C for 20 min to solidify the outer agarose layer.

steps.title: Clean system after second phase
steps.instruction: Perform the same cleaning and sterilization routine described in step 7 (water rinse, 70 % isopropanol rinse, two 10‑min runs at 7 µL min⁻¹ with isopropanol then water, then stop pumps). The system is now ready for the next experiment.

description: Fig. 1 depicts the general procedure to generate agarose-solidified (w/w/o) double emulsion using the commercially available microfluidic ‘μEncapsulator System’ (Dolomite Microfluidics), including solution and microfluidics system preparation (work package 1), generation of agarose-solidified (w/o) emulsion (first phase, work package 2), an emulsion-breaking and washing step of the first phase (work package 3), and the generation of the final agarose-solidified (w/w/o) double emulsions (work package 4). Work package 3 is critical for this application, especially while working with cell cultures. The emulsion of the solidified agarose and the fluorocarbon oil NovecTM 7500 stabilized with Pico-SurfTM 1 (first phase) needs to be de-emulsified, since otherwise in the end both agarose phases would be separated by a diffusion barrier not fully understood [12,13]. The emulsion-breaking results in release of the first phase content into the aqueous phase that did not get stuck within the agarose, e.g., still motile cells. As a solution to separate agarose-solidified droplets of the first phase from other compartments, we designed a washing step based on density gradient centrifugation using Nycodenz®. Some agarose-solidified double emulsion examples are shown in Fig. 6. They are ∼55 µm in diameter with a volume of ∼87 pL and they can be empty (Fig. 6a) or e.g., carry bacteria. In our case we did experiments with first phases carrying single E. coli DH5α cells, incubated for a few hours and engulfed with a second agarose layer (Fig. 6b–e). An encapsulation of dsRed producing E. coli DH5α pFU96 cells in the first phase and GFP producing E. coli DH5α pFU95 cells in the outer layer (Fig. 6f) shows how cells are distributed in both compartments. Usually the microfluidics setup and all chemicals are prepared within half an hour. A single encapsulation generating the first or second phase takes with preparation about 45 min.
